subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and configured tools?
rationale: The implementation shape is clear, but this changes Slack access-control semantics and the issue itself calls out private shared-channel/Slack Connect caveats.

options.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, and tests while preserving existing defaults unless a separate migration is approved.

options.title: Reject private-channel boundary
options.body: Keep explicit Slack channel ID allowlists as the only non-open group authorization mode and document private/shared channels as insufficient trust boundaries.

options.title: Defer to broader access-control design
options.body: Track the idea under a broader channel authorization model if maintainers want a cross-channel policy rather than a Slack-specific value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, and tests while preserving existing defaults unless a separate migration is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue and is the strongest available routing signal for the Slack/security product decision.
